sentences.text:
This application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking the following reliefs:-
Bharti Jha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158452971/

sentences.text:
" 1. To quash the impugned FIR No.0046/2023, dated 01.08.2023, registered at Mahila Police Thana, Shahdol, District Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh (Annexure P/1)
registered against the petitioners in the interest of justice.

2. To Quash the entire subsequent criminal proceedings arising out of the FIR, in the interest of justice."
2.
It is submitted by counsel for applicant that she is the sister-in-law of respondent No. 2.
The respondent No. 2 lodged an FIR on the allegations that she got married to Anil Jha on 15.11.2021.
After her marriage, her husband and his family members started abusing and use to pass taunts and assault her on the ground of bringing less dowry.

In order to save her marital life, she was tolerating the cruelty meted out to her by her husband with a hope and belief that on one day the behavior of her husband would improve but it did not happen and the demand of dowry by her husband went on.
In the meanwhile, she gave birth to a girl child on 08.09.2022.
The applicant also used to extend a threat that she would kill respondent No. 2 and her daughter by burning and also used to claim that no one can cause any harm to her.
In the month of 2023, her husband came to her parental home and also demanded dowry and on account of non fulfillment of demand of dowry, he started assaulting her and also dragged her on the road.
On account of timely intervention by the by passers, she survived otherwise her husband would have killed her.
Thereafter, her husband took her back to her matrimonial house.
In the meanwhile, respondent No. 2 again got pregnant and in spite of resistance by respondent No. 2, he continued to have physical relationship with her.
When she got herself medically examined, then it was found that she is carrying the pregnancy of one month.
When her husband came to know about that, then he started claiming that he is not the father of the child and he would sell the child.
He also started alleging that the biological father of the child is the younger brother of respondent No. 2.
On 28.07.2023, her husband gave a kick in her stomach as a result she suffered abortion.

It was further alleged that applicant No. 2 was also visiting her house frequently and was also assaulting her and used to allege that whenever respondent No. 2 goes to her parental home, then she comes back with pregnancy.
She was also insisting that the child does not belong to her brother and was alleging that in fact the child belongs to younger brother of respondent No. 2.
She was also insisting that respondent No. 2 should get the DNA test of the child.

It was further alleged that applicant is residing nearer to her matrimonial house and always challenges that respondent No. 2 may lodge the report but nobody can cause any harm to her and she also threatened that she would kill respondent No. 2 and her daughter and accordingly the FIR was lodged.

3. Challenging the FIR lodged by respondent No. 2, it is submitted by counsel for applicant that in fact applicant is the resident of Sri Ganganagar (Rajasthan) which is evident from the Aadhar Card which has been filed as Annexure-P/4.

It is further submitted that even otherwise for prosecuting the near and dear relatives of the husband of the complainant, the allegations must be clear and specific and the near and dear relative cannot be compelled to face the ordeal of trial on the basis of vague, omnibus and general allegations.
The allegations which have been made against applicant are general in nature, therefore, the FIR is liable to be quashed.

In support of his contention, counsel for applicant has also relied upon the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar Alias Sonam and others Vs. State of Bihar and Others, decided on 08.02.2022 in Criminal Bharti Jha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158452971/
2 Appeal No. 195/2022.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, the application is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State.
5. It is submitted that the FIR is not an encyclopedia.

Even otherwise, there are specific allegations that not only applicant is residing nearer to the matrimonial house of respondent No. 2 but she was continuously passing taunts with regard to the character of respondent No. 2 by alleging that she is carrying the child of her younger brother and the child does not belong to her husband and she was also extending a threat that she would kill respondent No. 2 and her child with a further challenge that nobody can cause any harm to applicant.
6.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
7. In the FIR, it is specifically mentioned that applicant is residing nearer to the matrimonial house of respondent No. 2.

The matrimonial house of respondent No. 2 is undisputedly situated in Jhansi,
whereas; applicant has claimed that she is the resident of Ward No. 16, Gurunanak Colony, Sri Karanpur, District Sri Ganganagar (Rajasthan).
To substantiate her contention with regard to her place of residence, applicant has relied upon the Aadhar Card as Annexure-P/4.

On the reverse side of the Aadhar Card, the address of applicant is mentioned which has been disclosed in the cause title but in the corner of the Aadhar Card, it is also mentioned that "details as on 02.12.2023".
The FIR in question was lodged on 01.08.2023 with a specific allegations that applicant is residing nearer to the matrimonial house of respondent No. 2 i.e. Jhansi.
Accordingly, the counsel for applicant was requested to clarify the meaning of the words "details as on 02.12.2023" as mentioned in the Aadhar Card.
It is submitted by counsel for applicant that it might be the date of downloading of the Aadhar Card.
However, the counsel could not state with authority that the Aadhar Card was not modified on 02.12.2023.

8. Be that whatever it may be.
9.
One thing is clear that Aadhar Card is a document of biometrics and it is neither a document of date of birth nor a document of residential address.

Accordingly, only on the basis of the Aadhar Card which also contains the words "details as on 02.12.2023", it is difficult for this Court to give a finding that applicant is the resident of Sri Ganganagar (Rajasthan).
No other supporting document(s) have been filed by the applicant to substantiate her place of resident.
The applicant has projected that she is a practicing lawyer.
Even the ID proof issued by the Bar Council of Rajasthan has not been placed on record.
Even the ID proof issued by the Bar Association of Sri Ganganagar has not been placed on record.
No other ID proof has been filed to show that applicant is residing in Ward No. 16, Gurunanak Colony, Sri Karanpur, District Sri Ganganagar (Rajasthan).

In view of the two self contradictory claims i.e. according to the complainant applicant is the resident of Jhansi,
whereas; according to applicant she is the resident Sri Ganganagar (Rajasthan) and in absence of any conclusive proof to show that applicant is residing Sri Ganganagar, it is difficult for this Court to accept the contention of applicant that she is the resident of Sri Ganganagar (Rajasthan).

Therefore,
this question is left open for adjudication by the trial Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as the question with regard to the prosecution of a near and dear relative of husband of the complainant is concerned, the law is very clear.

11. The Supreme Court in the case of Kans Raj v. State of Punjab, reported in (2000) 5 SCC 207,
Monju Roy v. State of W.B., reported in (2015) 13 SCC 693, Kahkashan Kausar Alias Sonam and others Vs. State of Bihar and Others, reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599, Geeta Mehrotra Vs. State of U.P., reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741, Preeti Gupta Vs. State of Jharkhand, reported in (2010) 7 SCC 667 etc has held that for prosecuting a near and dear relative of the husband of the complainant, the allegations must be specific and clear and the near and dear relatives cannot be prosecuted on the basis of vague, omnibus and general allegations.
12.

sentences.text: Therefore, the allegations made in the FIR shall be considered in the light of law laid down by Supreme Court with regard to prosecution of near and dear relative of the husband of the complainant.

In the FIR, it is specifically mentioned that immediately after the marriage, applicant was extending a threat to respondent No. 2 that she would kill her as well as her daughter and nobody would be able to cause any harm to her.

Thereafter, when respondent No. 2 got pregnant for the second time, it was alleged that applicant was alleging that the child belongs to the younger brother of respondent No. 2 and not the husband of respondent No. 2.

It is also alleged that she also use to assault her and also use to allege that whenever, respondent No. 2 goes to her parental home,
then she comes back with a pregnancy.
She was also insisting that respondent No. 2 should undergo the DNA test and she was also claiming that nobody can cause any harm to her.
All these incident took place sometimes in the month of June or July, 2023, whereas; the FIR was lodged on 1st of August, 2023.
Under these circumstances this Court is of considered opinion that there are specific and clear allegations of cruelty against applicant.
13. It is submitted by counsel for applicant that there is nothing on record to suggest that respondent No. 2 was being treated with cruelty by applicant on account of any demand of dowry.

14. Section 498-A of IPC reads as under:-
"498A. Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty.-Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman,
subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, "cruelty means"--
(a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to Bharti Jha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158452971/
4 meet such demand."
15.

entities.text: Bharti Jha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From plain reading of the definition of cruelty, it is clear that cruelty is not confined to demand of any valuable article but any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health of the woman would also amount to cruelty.
16. Alleging against the character of a woman would certainly fall within the category of cruelty.

17. Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that the FIR lodged by respondent No. 2 prima facie makes out an offence under Section 498-A of IPC.
18.
Accordingly, the application fails and is hereby dismissed.
